sections.h2: What does a Tennessee quitclaim deed do?
sections.html:
It hands over whatever the signer owns, with no assurance that the signer owns anything. Tennessee's revenue department describes a true quitclaim as passing only a "mere chance of title," and it contrasts that with a deed that conveys the property itself or gives a warranty.

Families use quitclaims to move a house between relatives, to add or drop a spouse, and to remove a name from a chain of ownership. Since no warranty rides along, anyone who accepts one from a stranger is leaning entirely on the title search. If you intend to sell, expect a title company to look harder at a house whose last transfer was a quitclaim than at one with a warranty deed behind it.

Whatever the deed type, it only gains public standing once the county register of deeds records it. That is the stage where Tennessee's tax, fee and formatting rules bite, and the sections below follow it step by step.

sections.h2: How much recording tax does a Tennessee quitclaim deed carry?
sections.html:
The state realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of value, which works out to $3.70 per $1,000. The grantee owes it, and the register in the receiving county collects it at the counter. The Department of Revenue rate page confirms the figure.

A quitclaim differs in what the rate is multiplied by. Shelby County's register states that only the consideration actually given is used for a quitclaim, citing Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409(a)(1)(D). A quitclaim signed for $10 between relatives therefore produces a tiny bill, while a deed worded to reach the property itself is taxed on its worth.

How a deed's wording picks the tax base
What the deed says or doesTax baseSource
Passes only the signer's chance of titleConsideration givenRevenue help article REC-20; Shelby County Register
Contains a habendum clause ("to have and to hold") or says "in fee simple (absolute)"Fair market valueRevenue help article REC-20
Falls in a statutory exemptionNo tax and no oath of valueShelby County Register, citing 67-4-409(a)(1)(E)

As a worked example, a $250,000 house taxed at full value would owe $925 (250,000 times 0.0037). The same house conveyed by a true quitclaim for $10 of consideration would owe pennies at that rate, and the register's page fees would still apply.

sections.h2: Which quitclaim wording pushes the tax up to fair market value?
sections.html:
Any phrase that signals an intent to convey the land itself, or that promises title, shifts the base from consideration to value. Revenue's two examples are the habendum clause and "in fee simple (absolute)," and it says those are samples rather than a closed list.

Drafting is therefore part of tax planning. A downloaded form with warranty-style phrases can turn a cheap transfer into an expensive one, so ask whoever prepares the deed to strip them out if you want the lower base. Deeds drawn by an attorney or title company should already match the treatment you expect.

  • Read the granting clause for words that promise good title.
  • Look for a habendum clause or fee simple language.
  • Make sure the stated consideration matches what changed hands.
  • Ask the register to explain the tax before you leave the deed there.

sections.h2: How is fair market value measured when the deed is taxed on value?
sections.html:
Revenue accepts the base on the assessor's books or a recent appraisal that the assessor has accepted in a dispute over the base. A lower figure invites an audit, with penalties and interest on anything found owing.

So the appraised value on your county roll is the safest starting number. If you think it runs high, an assessor-approved appraisal is the route to challenge it. Request the parcel's current appraisal from the county assessor before the deed is drawn, so the sworn value and the tax paid agree.

sections.h2: What paperwork does a register want with a quitclaim deed?
sections.html:
Shelby County's register publishes a checklist with statute cites for each line, and the list marks every line below as applying to quitclaim deeds. Other counties draw on the same Tennessee statutes, though each register runs its own counter.

  • The names of both the grantor and the grantee.
  • A sworn statement of value whenever the deed is taxable.
  • A derivation clause naming how the grantor took title, and the street address unless the land is vacant.
  • The owner's name and address, plus whoever pays the property tax bill.
  • The ward, block and parcel number and a full legal description.
  • The name and address of whoever prepared the deed (Tenn. Code Ann. 66-24-115).
  • Notarized signatures and an original, unless the filing goes in electronically.

Davidson County's fee page repeats the preparer rule in one sentence: every document except releases and charters must show who drafted it. Phone the register where the house is located and ask how that office takes submissions before you drive over with a deed.

sections.h2: What will filing a quitclaim deed set you back in Nashville and Memphis?
sections.html:
Fees flow from Tenn. Code Ann. 8-21-1001. Davidson County puts warranty and quitclaim deeds under "all other documents" at $5 a page, a $10 floor and a $2 data processing charge. Shelby County bills $10 for the first two pages and $5 for each later page, with its own data processing line.

  • Davidson County adds a $1 probate fee that applies only when state tax is paid.
  • Shelby County adds a $1 register fee under the same condition.
  • The $0.37 per $100 tax in both counties is billed on top of the page fees.

Other counties publish their own schedules, so ask the register of the county that holds your parcel for the current numbers.

sections.h2: Which transfers owe no recording tax?
sections.html:
Several do, and Shelby County's guide lists them under 67-4-409(a)(1). Where a deed falls in an exempt class, no oath of value is demanded either.

  • One spouse conveying to the other to create or end a tenancy by the entirety.
  • Deeds that settle property between divorcing spouses.
  • Moves into a revocable living trust by its creator or the creator's spouse, and moves back out.
  • An executor's deed that carries out a devise in a will.

An exemption removes the tax and the oath. It leaves the fee schedule and the formatting rules in place.

sections.h2: Did Tennessee change what registers can record in 2026?
sections.html:
It did. Public Chapter 865 amends Tenn. Code Ann. 66-24-101(a), and the University of Tennessee's County Technical Assistance Service lists it in its 2026 index of acts with an April 27, 2026 effective date.

A bond for conveying real or personal property now needs every bound party's authenticated signature and the bond's expiration date to be recordable. Sale agreements, contracts, memoranda and abstracts for real property need the authenticated signatures of the owner (or the owner's attorney-in-fact or court-appointed representative) and the proposed purchaser, plus an expiration date. A quitclaim deed is a separate instrument, yet a seller who records a contract or memorandum should plan around the stricter standard.

faqs.q: Who has to pay Tennessee's tax on a quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: The grantee. Revenue's help article says the person receiving the interest pays, and that the register of the county where the deed is recorded collects it.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed need a sworn statement of value?
faqs.a: Yes when the deed is taxable. Shelby County's checklist lists an affidavit of value under 67-4-409(a)(6)(A) and says exempt transactions need no oath.

faqs.q: Can spouses use a quitclaim without paying tax?
faqs.a: A conveyance from one spouse to the other that creates or ends a tenancy by the entirety is exempt, and so are deeds between divorcing spouses. The exemptions are narrow, so check your facts with the register or an attorney.

faqs.q: What does the clerk charge in Nashville to file a quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: Davidson County charges $5 a page with a $10 minimum and a $2 data processing fee. A $1 probate fee and the $0.37 per $100 transfer tax come on top when state tax is due.

faqs.q: Will a register take a photocopy of my quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: Generally no. Shelby County asks for an original unless the filing is made electronically, so ask your own register whether it offers e-filing.
